Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Every protection at once**: kagex-release can now sign a release that's also encrypted with its file names hidden (0.9.0 refused Signing with *Hide names*). The game checks `data.xpc` and the small `startup.tjs` that opens it before it starts. A game with its own `data/system` needs this release's framework for that (the check says so)
- **Search, going back and Replay on the web, Android and iOS**: the sample's packages there now carry its compiled scenarios. They can't compile them as they play, so in 0.9.0 the demos played from the scripts, and Search found nothing, BACK did nothing and Replay had no scenes
- kagex-release 0.9.1 downloads the 0.9.1 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.9.1/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
